newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil complex ends lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil complex ends lower on profit-taking.

text.p: The NYMEX oil complex ended lower Monday on profit-taking after a rally on Friday absorbed the upside a cold spell in the U.S. Northeast would have on prices, traders said.
"I think we were in an overbought situation after Friday," said James Cordier, trader at Allendale Inc in Florida. The U.S. Northeast is the largest heating oil market in the world.
December heating oil settled 0.58 cent lower a gallon at 68.35 cents. December crude followed heating oil down, ending 22
December gasoline settled off 0.25 cent a gallon at 65.02 cents, recovering from lower levels on strength in the U.S. Gulf cash market.
Traders attributed the strength to at least one major player pushing up the price amid particulary quiet trade due to the American Petroleum Institute's annual meeting in Washington D.C.
Cash traders were also buying supply amid low stocks to make a shipping deadline set by Colonial Pipeline, the major pipeline between Houston and the New York Harbor, traders said.
"There is a squeeze going on because today is the last day of the 32nd (shipping) cycle. On top of that, there is not a lot of supply," said a dealer.

Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis forecasted temperatures 11 to 15 degrees below normal through Friday in the U.S. Northeast that is expected to result in above average heating oil demand by consumers.
But, Davis said the cold spell should end by weekend with near to slightly above normal temperatures expected to hit the region by next week.

"The colder weather caused this upward correction (on Friday), but frankly we knew temperatures would be getting colder eventually so it (the rally) just ran out of steam," said ING Derivatives analyst Tom Bentz.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
